text: Technology theme universe should remain centered on AI/cloud infrastructure as a system, with reference leaders used for demand validation and underfollowed suppliers prioritized for discovery.
Highest-confidence Layer 1 chokepoint cluster is advanced packaging, HBM backend, OSAT capacity, inspection/metrology, probe cards, and backend test equipment.

CPO and silicon-photonics upstream manufacturing stack is a promising underfollowed lane, especially MOCVD, etch/deposition, optical connectivity, bonding, substrates, and test, but requires primary-source validation.
Power/cooling/grid and second-order cloud software lanes are underbuilt relative to semiconductor packaging/test and need additional Layer 2 searches for small/mid-cap names with primary evidence.
Before Layer 2 ranking, refresh market caps, analyst coverage, liquidity, valuation, backlog, customer concentration, segment revenue, and direct AI exposure for every candidate.
Keep low-attention hypothesis names such as Cohu, Kulicke & Soffa, Oxford Instruments, Huber+Suhner, and Powertech in the universe if they carry explicit evidence-to-verify and falsification hooks.

For the Technology theme, treat AI infrastructure as a multi-layer system: compute demand pulls through HBM, advanced packaging, substrates, inspection/metrology, test, optical networking, data-center power/cooling, grid equipment, turbines, transmission, and upstream gas.

Highest-priority chokepoint candidates in this Layer 2A map are ABF film allocation, advanced substrates, customer certification gates, advanced packaging capacity/yield, inspection/metrology, HBM-related probe/test, and grid equipment.

Low-attention bottleneck value may hide in niche semiconductor equipment, probe cards, backend test handlers/contactors, memory-backend OSAT overflow, photonics manufacturing tools, optical connectivity, transmission contractors, and gas/pipeline infrastructure.

Important catalysts to monitor are customer-funded substrate capacity, HBM/test-related backlog, advanced-packaging yield/customer validation, CPO production deployments, data-center power interconnection announcements, grid-equipment lead times, and gas-turbine delivery constraints.

Before any company ranking, verify non-primary Substack claims against filings, earnings calls, annual reports, customer disclosures, backlog data, capex announcements, and segment revenue/margin evidence.

The map currently has better evidence for semiconductor packaging/metrology/test nodes than for upstream gas and pipeline AI pull-through; energy-infrastructure nodes should remain inference or speculation until contract-level or project-level evidence is gathered.

CAMT should be tracked as an underfollowed inspection/metrology supplier tied to advanced packaging, HBM, hybrid bonding, and high-density micro-bump yield control. Key survival test: multi-customer 2026 order durability and HBM/advanced-packaging revenue visibility.

FORM should be tracked as an underfollowed HBM known-good-die and wafer-probe-card node. Key survival test: sustained HBM probe-card revenue, backlog, pricing, and margin expansion rather than one-time qualification demand.

ONTO should be tracked as an underfollowed process-control, inspection/metrology, and advanced-packaging lithography supplier. Key survival test: broadening HBM/advanced-packaging customer adoption beyond a few volume purchase agreements.
AMKR should remain a reference/control OSAT capacity name for advanced packaging and package/test capacity rather than the primary underfollowed alpha target in this chunk.

KLIC is a second-order bonding/interconnect equipment hypothesis. It should not be upgraded without evidence of production orders in TCB, hybrid bonding, advanced memory, CPO, or heterogeneous integration.
AIXA.DE is a CPO/silicon-photonics upstream MOCVD/compound-epitaxy hypothesis. It requires evidence that datacom/photonics/CPO orders are material relative to power electronics or LED cycles.
OXIG.L is a niche III-V etch/deposition and photonics-tools hypothesis. Segment evidence must show semiconductor photonics order acceleration before it can survive later scoring.

HUBN.SW is an optical-connectivity/data-center-interconnect hypothesis. The AI relationship is plausible but currently weak until AI data-center, CPO, or high-density optical connectivity is visible in segment growth or backlog.
COHU is a backend test-handler/contactor/thermal-test hypothesis. It requires proof that AI/HBM/GPU-related demand is material enough to offset weaker legacy semiconductor end markets.

6239.TW should be tracked as an underfollowed memory-backend OSAT/FOPLP hypothesis. Current evidence is mostly external search context, so company filings, monthly revenue, margins, customer validation, and capex evidence are required before upgrade.

Primary-source validation is missing for most company-specific claims in this chunk. Later layers should prioritize annual reports, exchange filings, earnings-call transcripts, investor decks, order/backlog disclosures, customer announcements, and segment revenue bridges.

Market-pricing checks are not yet completed: refresh market cap, valuation multiples, revenue growth expectations, estimate revisions, short interest, liquidity, analyst coverage, and ownership quality before ranking this chunk for investability.
This chunk is mostly reference leaders; the most useful role of NVDA, TSM, AVGO, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, and ETN is demand validation, not alpha generation.
The clearest underfollowed chokepoints surfaced by this chunk are KLA in process control, IBIDF in substrates and ABF allocation, and 6239.TW in advanced packaging and FOPLP.
Primary-source confirmation is still missing for Powertech FOPLP validation, customer names, yields, and any CPO progress.
Primary-source confirmation is still missing for Ibiden customer advance payments, co-funded capex, and the exact severity of ABF film allocation constraints.
The data-center power and grid lane is still underexpanded below ETN; smaller contractors, transmission names, and power electronics suppliers should be searched next.

NET mapped to second-order AI/cloud software via edge networking, application security, connectivity, and developer platform; retain as hypothesis pending proof of AI inference/developer workload monetization, DBNR durability, and capex efficiency.

DDOG mapped to observability, AI operations, cloud complexity, and security software; strongest direct software relationship in this chunk, but still requires AI-specific usage and net retention evidence before being treated as a durable chokepoint.
S mapped to AI-enabled endpoint/cloud/security automation as an underfollowed mid-cap hypothesis; evidence supports ARR growth and AI-security positioning but not yet causal AI-driven growth.
HCP should be removed from the standalone public-company universe because IBM completed the HashiCorp acquisition on 2025-02-27.
IBM may be used only as a reference mapping for HashiCorp infrastructure automation exposure; do not treat it as an underfollowed pure-play candidate.

Software lane requires stronger Layer 2C evidence: AI-specific revenue contribution, cohort expansion, DBNR or NRR trends, customer case studies, gross margin/capex sensitivity, pricing power, and competitive displacement versus hyperscaler-native tools or open-source alternatives.

Market-pricing checks are still missing for NET, DDOG, S, and IBM: refresh current market cap, EV/revenue, revenue-growth expectations, analyst coverage, short interest, ownership quality, and whether AI exposure is already fully priced.
